SideSpeed 0.8.1 can update your sideloaded apps, and the Companion now talks to TVs over an encrypted connection.

## What's new
- **Update now for sideloaded apps.** When a newer version of an app you sideloaded is out, the app's screen can offer **Update now**. SideSpeed downloads it, checks it is the same app with a newer version and the same signing key, then installs it. Your data in the app stays. It only updates apps you already have, one press at a time, and never installs new apps.
- **Encrypted connection to the TV.** On TVs with Wireless debugging, the Companion pairs once with a code and then uses an encrypted connection. If the port changes, it finds the TV again on its own. If it can't, Home says to turn Wireless debugging back on, with **Try again** and a place to type the port.
- **The older connection needs your OK.** A TV that can't use an encrypted connection can still connect the older way, after you agree to it. Anyone on your network could see or change the commands it sends, and could send their own while it is connected. TVs you added before this update wait for that choice before the Companion contacts them. If one of them can use an encrypted connection, Home asks you to pair it instead.
- **Each TV proves it's the one you added.** When you add a TV, the Companion leaves a secret on it. Before any other command, the TV has to show it still holds that secret. A TV that fails is not contacted again in the background.

## Security fixes
- The TV app checks its helper on every connection, so another app can't pretend to be it.
- The helper's log can only be read by the helper.
- The Companion checks the network again before every TV call, so it stops when you leave your Trusted Network.
- A Trusted Network is matched more strictly. If the Companion knows your router's hardware address, it must match. If it doesn't (always on Android, and often on a Mac), the network's DNS servers must be exactly the ones you saved. Tailscale's own DNS addresses and IPv6 DNS servers are left out of that comparison.
- Pairing a saved TV again proves it first and keeps its secret. Pairing only works on a Trusted Network.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/DevJardins/SideSpeed/blob/main/SECURITY.md) explains what protects what, and the known limits.

**After updating:** start the helper again (on Google TV, open SideSpeed; on Fire TV, use the Companion). In the Companion, each TV you added before needs one choice: pair it for the encrypted connection, or allow the older one.

**If your Trusted Network is no longer recognised:** your router may hand out different DNS servers than when you saved it. Add it again in Settings with **Add as Trusted Network**, then add your TVs to it again.

## Downloads
**On the TV:** open the Downloader app and enter code **3503400**, or go to `sidespeed.app/tv`. Both always get the latest SideSpeed APK.

**Companion:** open `sidespeed.app/phone` on your phone, or see [sidespeed.app](https://sidespeed.app) for the desktop installers.

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `SideSpeed-0.8.1.apk` (also as `SideSpeed.apk`) | The TV app (Android TV, Google TV, Fire TV with Fire OS) |
| `SideSpeed-Companion-0.8.1.apk` (also as `SideSpeed-Companion.apk`) | The companion for Android phones |
| `SideSpeed-Companion-0.8.1-macos-arm64.dmg` | The companion for macOS (Apple silicon) |
| `SideSpeed-Companion-0.8.1-windows-x64.msi` | The companion for Windows |
| `SideSpeed-Companion-0.8.1-linux-amd64.deb` / `-x86_64.rpm` | The companion for Linux |
